NEXORA AI // SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE
Engineering Verification Report

01 // Executive Summary

NEXORA AI is a full-stack, commercial-grade multimodal intelligence platform engineered specifically for modern desktop environments. The platform orchestrates state-of-the-art Large Language Models (Google Gemini Flash & Pro), local computer vision, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) across multi-format documents, generative art synthesis (Flux.1), motion video generation (OpenCV/FFmpeg), and official YouTube player embedding with interactive timestamp seeking.

02 // System Architecture Overview

The system follows a modular decoupled client-server architecture. The backend is powered by FastAPI and Uvicorn, utilizing asynchronous non-blocking event loops for high-throughput multimodal streaming. The frontend is built with high-performance vanilla ES6+ JavaScript, CSS3 Glassmorphism, and a 3D WebGL rendering engine powered by Three.js.

Multi-Tier Architecture Diagram

Architectural Layer Component Modules Engineered Capabilities
Client Presentation Chat Studio, Image Studio, Video Studio, Generated Media Gallery, Three.js Robot Real-time WebGL humanoid animations, responsive iframe embeds, audio spectrum visuals
API Gateway Layer FastAPI Routers: /api/chat, /api/media, /api/models, /api/files Pydantic data validation, SSE response streaming, CORS headers, SSRF network filters
Multimodal AI Engine Google GenAI SDK (Gemini), Web Media Service, RAG Vector Knowledge Base Vision inspection, audio transcription, YouTube captions, semantic document search
Synthesis Studios Flux.1 Generative Engine, Nexora Motion Engine (FFmpeg & OpenCV) Batch multi-image generation (1–4x), universal H.264 MP4 & WebM VP8 rendering
Persistence Layer SQLAlchemy ORM, SQLite (nexora.db), Media Disk Storage Relational conversations, message histories, upload staging, generated assets metadata

03 // Core Technology Stack

Backend & AI Frameworks

• FastAPI 0.115+ & Uvicorn: Asynchronous HTTP & SSE engine
• Google GenAI SDK: Native binary multimodal inference
• SQLAlchemy & SQLite: Session & media persistence
• YouTubeTranscriptApi & BS4: Captions & Open Graph parsing
• FFmpeg & OpenCV: Hardware-accelerated video synthesis

Frontend & Graphics Systems

• Three.js (WebGL): 3D humanoid robot with 6 procedural states
• Hls.js: HTTP Live Streaming (.m3u8) video playback
• Marked.js & Highlight.js: Markdown & syntax highlighting
• Web Audio & Speech API: Speech recognition & voice TTS
• CSS3 Glassmorphism: Dark cybernetic theme with parallax

03 // Features & Multimodal Capabilities

1. Interactive 3D Humanoid Robot Assistant

Prominently mounted on the right viewport (~38% width), the WebGL Three.js robot features PBR metallic materials, cyan/purple ocular LED visor, and glowing arc reactor. It transitions smoothly between 6 synchronized states: idle (levitation), thinking (head tilt + orbiting rings), speaking (jaw oscillation + chest pulse), listening, greeting, and processing, with real-time mouse cursor parallax tracking.

2. YouTube Integration & Interactive Timestamps

Pastes of YouTube URLs (standard, shorts, youtu.be) automatically trigger oEmbed metadata extraction and official iframe embedding (enablejsapi=1). Captions are parsed via youtube-transcript-api. When the AI cites moments (e.g. [00:52]), they render as interactive buttons (⏱️ 00:52) that dispatch seek events to the embedded player.

Figure 3.1: Actual Application Screenshot — Embedded YouTube Player, Interactive Timestamps, and 3D Robot.

3. Vision, OCR & Document RAG

• Supports JPG, PNG, WEBP multi-image uploads.
• Native binary transmission for OCR, scene layout, and chart analysis.
• Ingests PDF, Word DOCX, CSV with vector embedding & cosine search.
• Strict XML sandbox boundaries against prompt injection.

4. Generative Image & Video Studios

• Image Studio: Flux.1 text-to-image with 1–4 batch variations.
• Video Studio: Text-to-video and image-to-video with camera motion.
• Dual H.264 MP4 and WebM VP8 export with direct file downloads.
• Persistent media gallery with SQLite metadata storage.

5. Web Media Streaming & SSRF Defense

• Universal Video: Plays direct MP4, WebM, and HLS (.m3u8) streams via Hls.js.
• Open Graph Previews: Scrapes article titles, descriptions, social images, and favicons for contextual Q&A.
• Enterprise SSRF Security: Blocks loopback (127.0.0.1), RFC 1918 private IPs (10.0.0.0/8, 192.168.0.0/16), and AWS/cloud metadata (169.254.169.254).

06 // Installation & Environment Setup

NEXORA AI runs locally on Windows without requiring complex container setups. Ensure Python 3.10+ is installed and configured in the system environment PATH.

1. Clone & Install Dependencies

git clone https://github.com/akankshaupadhyay665-netizen/nexoraAI_multimodal_Chatbot.git cd nexoraAI_multimodal_Chatbot pip install -r requirements.txt

2. Configure Environment Secrets (.env)

Copy .env.example to .env and add your Google Gemini API key:

# .env - Nexora AI Configuration HOST=127.0.0.1 PORT=8000 FRONTEND_PORT=5500 GEMINI_API_KEY=your_google_gemini_api_key_here UPLOAD_DIR=backend/storage/uploads GENERATED_IMAGE_DIR=backend/storage/generated_images GENERATED_VIDEO_DIR=backend/storage/generated_videos DATABASE_URL=sqlite:///./nexora.db

07 // Application Launch Procedures

Method A: One-Click Desktop Launch (Recommended)

Double-click start.bat in the project root directory. It automatically starts both the FastAPI backend server on port 8000 and the frontend HTTP server on port 5500, then opens your default browser.

Method B: Manual Terminal Execution
# Terminal 1: Launch FastAPI Backend Server python -m uvicorn backend.main:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 # Terminal 2: Launch Frontend Application Server python serve_frontend.py
Access URLs:
• Web Application Interface: http://127.0.0.1:5500
• Backend API Documentation (Swagger): http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs
